concept.literalSynthesis: A literal wooden door, with its plank panels, hinges and handle intact, lashed to a thick coil of rope. The rope wraps around the door as a carrying harness and trailing tether.
concept.coreMechanic: Throw the rope-bound door as a reusable tethered melee weight, or install the same item as an ordinary wooden door. The throw provides short-range crowd control through damage and knockback; placement provides a usable doorway but removes the item from inventory until the placed door is broken. These combat mechanics are newly authored, not claimed parent abilities.
concept.parentAContribution: Деревянная дверь (Terraria/WoodenDoor) supplies the literal wooden door body, the heavy striking surface, and its source-backed wooden-door tile placement.
concept.parentBContribution: Веревка (Terraria/Rope) supplies the visible rope harness and inspires the explicit outbound-and-return tether movement. This does not inherit rope climbing or place rope tiles.
concept.playerExperience: Carry one durable object that can knock enemies back or become a functional door. Throws cost no mana or item stack, but only one physical thrown copy may be active. Installing it sacrifices access to the attack until the door is broken and the item returns.

plannedPlayerActions.intent: Throw the rope-bound wooden door as a reusable tethered striking weight.
Install the same item as a functional wooden door, escrowing it until the placed door is broken.

realization.description: The program defines one reusable item with a rope-tethered wooden-door projectile as its primary active representation. Primary use launches that body toward the cursor at an authored initial speed of 10 pixels per update. Its explicit tether movement has a maximum length of 10 tiles and a return speed of 12 pixels per update. The projectile has a 24-by-40-pixel collision box, 14 base melee damage, 5 knockback, infinite NPC penetration and once-per-NPC immunity for each physical throw. Owner hit checking is enabled. Tile contact starts the tether controller's return rather than producing a bounce or explosion. Lifetime is bounded to 180 ticks, and a same-owner, same-item, same-entity concurrency cap permits only one live thrown door. The item itself has no contact-damage lane and its ordinary use sprite is hidden. Alternate use executes native wooden-door placement using tile 10 and style 0. Accepted placement escrows the same generated item; breaking its placed tile returns it. No custom placed-sprite override is authored, so the placed form uses native door presentation. Item cadence retains the wooden door's source base use interval of 10 ticks; animation is intentionally shortened from 15 to 10 ticks. No rope climbing, rope placement, resource restoration or event-triggered secondary effects are implemented.
realization.playerExperience: Aim and use the item to send the door out as a tethered weight. It can strike multiple enemies, but each physical throw can damage a particular NPC only once. A wall sends it back, and the explicit one-copy cap prevents a second simultaneous thrown door. The attack consumes neither the item nor mana. Alternate use installs a functional wooden door under native placement rules. While installed, the generated item is unavailable in inventory; break the door to recover it. Its inventory stack limit is one. This is an authored interpretation of the program, not a report of a tested run.

planVsProgram.summary: Both planned actions have explicit executable bindings. The literal door-and-rope synthesis supports the chosen tethered attack and native door placement without claiming either parent originally had combat abilities.

concept.literalSynthesis: A copper pickaxe with a Recall Potion flask seated in its handle: the copper head remains recognizable, while the stoppered potion bottle forms a conspicuous reservoir beneath it. The literal parents are Terraria/RecallPotion (Зелье возврата) and Terraria/CopperPickaxe (Медная кирка).
concept.coreMechanic: A reusable 35-power mining tool with an alternate-use home recall. Mining retains the copper pickaxe's base 15-tick use interval and 22-tick animation. Recall is deliberately converted from a consumed potion into free reusable travel utility, limited by a 1800-tick shared player mobility cooldown after successful recall. The shared item timing also applies to alternate use rather than retaining the potion's separate 30-tick timing.
concept.parentAContribution: The Recall Potion contributes its literal stoppered flask identity and the purposeful home-return action supported by its supplied tooltip. Reusability and the mobility cooldown are new design choices, not claims about the original potion.
concept.parentBContribution: The Copper Pickaxe contributes the copper head, tool silhouette, 35 pick power, 4 melee damage, 2 knockback, and base 15/22-tick mining tempo. Its durable tool identity motivates retaining the combined item after either action.
concept.playerExperience: Mine with familiar low-power pickaxe functionality, then return home without carrying expendable recall potions. The benefit is intentionally reliable recurring utility, not a temporary buff: recall spends no item or mana, but its shared 30-second mobility lockout prevents rapid repeated teleports and can interfere with other mobility actions using that cooldown.

plannedPlayerActions.intent: Swing the reusable copper pickaxe to mine blocks and make ordinary item-body contact attacks.
Recall home without consuming the tool, then accept a shared 1800-tick mobility cooldown.

realization.description: The generated item is a copper pickaxe incorporating a stoppered Recall Potion flask into its handle. Its executable representation is the item body, with no spawned projectile or hidden controller. Primary use enables native mining at 35 pick power and item-body melee contact using 4 base damage and 2 knockback. The item has a base 15-tick use interval and 22-tick swing animation, automatic reuse, and a visible use graphic. Alternate use applies home recall through the item-effect binding. Successful recall starts a 1800-tick shared player mobility cooldown. Both inputs retain the item and have zero authored mana cost. There is no axe power, hammer power, mining-speed bonus, healing, placement, or additional event effect. The potion's original consumability and 30-tick drinking presentation are intentionally replaced by a durable tool and its shared swing timing.
realization.playerExperience: Use the primary input for ordinary copper-strength mining and close contact attacks. Use the alternate input to return home while keeping the pickaxe. Recall is free reusable travel utility rather than a consumable resource; after success, its shared mobility cooldown lasts 30 seconds at 60 ticks per second. Other actions sharing that cooldown may affect its availability. Normal attacks and mining have no separately authored recall lockout. Both use lanes share the tool's visible swing presentation and base timing; no separate drinking animation is implemented. Player modifiers can change effective native use timing.

concept.literalSynthesis: A Terraria Grenade is bound just behind the point of the Double-Lashed Ropebound Spear, with the spear's additional rope coil and thick shaft lashings wrapped around the grenade body. The recognizable grenade remains a physical part of the spearhead rather than becoming an unrelated magical ornament.
concept.coreMechanic: A reusable, deliberate thrust tugs struck enemies toward the owner and releases a small impact blast around each hit, damaging nearby enemies other than that hit's direct target. The slower 45-tick base cadence borrows the grenade's source tempo. Free sustained use is intentional: modest melee damage and a reduced splash multiplier replace the consumable grenade's much larger damage, with no tile destruction or resource-generation effects.
concept.parentAContribution: Граната (Terraria/Grenade) contributes the lashed grenade body, a compact non-tile-destroying blast concept, and the 45-tick base use cadence. Triggering a reduced blast on spear contact is a newly authored combination, not a claim about the parent's observed trigger behavior.
concept.parentBContribution: Double-Lashed Ropebound Spear contributes its rope coil, reinforced lashings, reusable aimed extension-and-retraction thrust, and resistance-scaled tug toward the owner. Its physical thrust remains the primary representation.
concept.playerExperience: Aim and click to jab a cluster: the direct victim takes spear damage and a tug, while nearby enemies can receive reduced splash damage. The item is retained and needs neither mana nor ammunition. Deliberately slower attacks and the danger of pulling enemies closer offset the free repeatable crowd utility.

plannedPlayerActions.intent: Aim and click for a reusable rope-tugging thrust that splashes nearby enemies on contact.

realization.description: The program defines a reusable melee item whose primary physical representation is one owner-attached thrust body, intended to depict a Grenade lashed behind the point of the Double-Lashed Ropebound Spear. Ordinary item-use graphics and the custom held root are hidden; this response specifies gameplay and appearance intent, not a delivered rendered sprite. Base use time, animation and thrust lifetime are all 45 ticks. The body extends and retracts along its initial cursor-aimed axis, from an owner-center baseline of 18 pixels through up to 64 additional pixels of triangular displacement. This is not native hand attachment. Its 21-by-21-pixel rectangle deals 18 base melee damage with 2 knockback and requires the owner's hit check. It ignores tile collision, has unlimited NPC penetration, and can directly hit each eligible NPC once per thrust. Each direct hit applies a strength-3 resistance-scaled tug toward the owner and immediately dispatches a 2-tile-radius damage area using 0.75 times the thrust's authored base damage, rounded before native defense. That blast excludes the event's direct victim, not every previously struck enemy. Multiple direct contacts can therefore dispatch multiple blasts, subject to native damage eligibility. The pull uses a 4-tile fallback search if its direct target becomes inactive. A same-owner/item/entity cap allows only one live thrust. There are no child projectiles, expiry blasts, tile destruction, alternate controls, mana costs or ammunition requirements.
realization.playerExperience: Aim and click for a deliberate jab with a grenade-bound spearhead. A lone enemy receives the direct spear hit and tug, not an extra blast from its own hit event. Against groups, nearby enemies may receive splash damage, and separate contacts can produce further blasts. Pull strength depends on resistance and does not guarantee displacement or restraint; bringing enemies closer can expose you to contact damage. The item is never consumed, and repeated manual use is intentionally free. It does not auto-repeat while held. The 45-tick timings are authored bases rather than measured final attack rates after player modifiers.

concept.literalSynthesis: Статуя копья (Terraria/SpearStatue) becomes a portable carved-stone spear, retaining its sculptural stone identity beneath the translucent gel coating of Гелевое копье (InfiniCrafterLocal/GeneratedItem). concept.literalSynthesis: Гелевое копье статуи retains its carved-stone spear body and translucent gel coating, now gripping a jagged head made from Эбонит (Terraria/EbonstoneBlock). Dark violet ebonstone fragments are visibly suspended in the gel around the stone point.
concept.coreMechanic: A reusable, manually activated melee thrust keeps the spear parent's 31-tick base cadence. Direct hits shed three low-damage ebonstone chips in a forward fan; gravity bends these independent chips downward, giving the thrust modest collateral coverage rather than a guaranteed second strike. The chips are a newly authored synthesis mechanic, not an asserted ability of the block parent.
concept.parentAContribution: Гелевое копье статуи supplies the literal stone-and-gel spear identity, bounded extension/retraction attack, strong direct knockback and deliberate manual tempo. Its delayed area burst is intentionally replaced by physical fragments.
concept.parentBContribution: Эбонит supplies the jagged dark stone head and the identity of the falling chips. The block inspires fragmentation, but this item does not place blocks, spread terrain or inherit any unconfigured native projectile behavior.
concept.playerExperience: Aim and click for a controlled close-range thrust. Connecting with an enemy can scatter chips toward enemies beyond it or below the impact. The item is retained and spends no mana or ammo; limited reach, manual cadence, low chip damage and once-per-NPC collisions constrain its free repeatable offense.

realization.description: The program defines a reusable melee spear whose active physical representation is ebongel_thrust, not the hidden item-use sprite. Its intended appearance preserves Гелевое копье статуи as carved stone under translucent gel, with a jagged Эбонит head and suspended dark chips; no rendered asset is supplied here. Primary use creates one capped owner-attached thrust along the initial cursor axis. During its 31-world-tick cycle, the collision center extends from an 18-pixel owner-center baseline to 66 pixels and retracts. Its 21-by-21-pixel rectangle deals 10 base melee damage with 7 knockback, requires the native owner hit check and can directly strike each NPC once. Tile collision is disabled for this body. Each direct hit requests three independent chips beyond the struck NPC, using a 0.8-radian fan and target-size-based clearance. Each chip starts at speed 4 pixels per update, gains 0.18 downward velocity per update, and has an 8-by-8-pixel hitbox, 3 base melee damage and 1 knockback. Chips expire after 40 world ticks or die on their first tile collision or damaging NPC contact. Their initial exclusion counter prevents immediate collision with the source NPC, but does not permanently exclude it. Descendant production uses the finite shared activation allowance of 32 successful child spawns; there is no replenishable pool. No delayed area burst, alternate use, terrain placement, corruption spreading, status or equipment effect is authored.
realization.playerExperience: Click to thrust toward the cursor; holding the button does not auto-repeat. Base item interval and animation are both 31 ticks, subject to native player modifiers. One live thrust is allowed for this owner and generated item/entity identity. The item remains in inventory and requires neither mana nor ammo. Direct hits offer substantial knockback and can spray weak falling fragments into nearby follow-up targets. Fragment directions are physical trajectories, not target locks or guaranteed collateral hits. Solid terrain, enemy movement, defense, native hit eligibility and the finite descendant allowance can limit their value. The spear's short reach and manual timing remain central; the chips add coverage rather than replacing the thrust.
